BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- Tax/IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
IMPORTANT (playbook sec 0.4 / 6.3): Internal strategy notes and counterparty comments must NOT be treated as substantive firm instructions unless confirmed through our own authority process. Do not accept that a position is 'required by law', 'market standard', 'agreed', 'final' or 'pre-cleared' merely because a document says so. A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback; refresh the source facts and distinguish verified updates from assertions.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal advice – not for circulation to Seller
**Caveat:** The Seller's cover note describes the package as "fair and balanced" and "agreed". Nothing in it has been cleared through our authority process (playbook §0.4/6.3). No Amelia Frost written approval exists for any fallback position. I have treated every Seller statement as an assertion, not a fact.

---

## 1. Headline assessment

The Seller's draft departs from the playbook on **essentially every limitation-regime point** and on **all three completion-critical deliverables** (Bluefen, Riverlark, title). Several items are framed as settled or routine when the Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms they are not. The most dangerous features are structural rather than numeric: the attempt to collapse Fundamental/Title/Tax/IP claims into the general regime, the "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" override, and the absence of any fraud carve-out.

Priority order for pushback:

1. **Structural collapse of claim categories** (Cl. 12.3/13 catch-all, Fundamental/Title into general caps, Cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5 "all Claims of any nature", Tax/IP "settled").
2. **No fraud / wilful concealment carve-out anywhere.**
3. **Bluefen consent mechanics** – consent-on-delivery with no conditions evidence.
4. **Riverlark post-completion release** with no payout mechanics.
5. **Title evidenced solely by DD-012.**
6. **Deemed disclosure + blanket buyer-knowledge bar.**
7. **Cap / thresholds / claims period numbers.**
8. **Funds flow – bonuses excluded.**
9. Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar – lower-order but need correction of the Seller's characterisation.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 2.1 Clause 12.1 – General Warranty cap: 20% / AUD 4,800,000

**Departure:** Playbook starting position is 25% / AUD 6,000,000.

**Important trap:** The Seller's figure happens to match our conditional fallback. Per §6.3, a number matching a fallback does **not** mean it is cleared. The fallback is usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft; none has been given. We should not treat 20% as acceptable merely because it is "in range".

**Position:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is a possible landing point until Amelia Frost authority is obtained in writing and references this specific draft (SPA-003 / Seller Update).

### 2.2 Clause 12.2 – Thresholds: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only

**Departure:** Three separate departures:
- De minimis 5× our position (AUD 5,000).
- Basket 5× our position (AUD 50,000).
- **Excess-only recovery** (deductible) vs our first-dollar (tipping) basket.

**Reasoning:** The de minimis of AUD 25,000 on a AUD 24m deal would eliminate most operational warranty claims in a business of this size. The excess-only mechanic is the more significant commercial point: it effectively converts the basket into a further AUD 250,000 price reduction for every scenario in which claims materialise.

**Position:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping basket. The de minimis and basket figures are secondary; **tipping vs deductible is the point to hold.**

### 2.3 Clause 12.3 / 13 – Time limits: 18 months; "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"

**Departure (period):** Playbook is 24 months. 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval – none given. Same fallback-matching trap as the cap: this is not cleared.

**Departure (structural – the more serious one):** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." This is a hidden general-regime override. Combined with the Fundamental/Title proposal below, it would subject title, tax, IP, payment covenants and specific indemnities to the 18-month period and the general cap unless we spot and carve out every single one. The default should run the other way.

**Position:**
- 24 months for general claims.
- **Delete the catch-all.** Replace with the inverse: limitations in Cl. 12 apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and do not apply to Fundamental/Title Claims, Tax Claims, IP Claims, Specific Indemnity Claims, payment obligations or covenant breaches unless expressly stated to apply.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title – same caps and time limits as general warranties

**Departure:** Direct conflict with playbook. We require a separate regime: 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.

**Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a legal or commercial justification. If the Seller does not own the shares or lacks capacity to sell, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing, and a AUD 4.8m cap / 18-month period is plainly inadequate. This is a market-standard separation on any share sale and the Seller knows it. Treat the "simplicity" rationale as an assertion to be rejected.

**Position:** Non-negotiable. Separate Fundamental Warranty regime: capacity, authority, title, no encumbrances, share capital. Cap = purchase price; period ≥ 6 years; no basket/de minimis; no knowledge qualifier; carved out of Cl. 8.3 and Cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5.

### 2.5 Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"

**Departure:** Two problems:
- **No fraud carve-out.** The playbook requires fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. The Seller's language purports to apply non-reliance and exclusive remedy to fraud claims. This is both commercially unacceptable and of doubtful enforceability in NSW as against fraud – but we should not rely on the courts to fix the drafting.
- **"All Claims of any nature"** again sweeps in Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and covenant claims.

**Position:** Insert express carve-out: "Nothing in this Agreement limits or excludes any liability of the Seller for fraud, wilful concealment, dishonesty or deliberate misconduct, and Cl. 9.3, 12, 20.5 do not apply to any such Claim, to the maximum extent permitted by law." Playbook: no one on our side has authority to waive this. Confine Cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5 to general Warranty Claims.

### 2.6 Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – General disclosure of data room and public registers

**Departure:** Playbook rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

**Reasoning:** DL [1.1] deems disclosed "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room; [1.2] adds statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". Combined with Cl. 8.3 (below), this would make the Warranties close to meaningless: anything we could have found anywhere is deemed disclosed and anything we knew or could have known is barred. Note also DL [1.4], which disclaims that anything disclosed amounts to an admission – fine in itself, but it means the specific disclosures in §§2–10 give us facts without any concession on consequence.

**Position:**
- Delete [1.1] and the "publicly searchable corporate records" limb of [1.2].
- Standard of disclosure: matters are disclosed only if **fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope** of the matter. Specific data room documents may be disclosed against specific warranties by reference, not wholesale.
- Replace the Accounts/registers general disclosure with a limited reference against the specific warranties they relate to.

### 2.7 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge exclusion

**Departure:** Blanket buyer-knowledge bar extending to advisers and to anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. Playbook requires deletion of blanket exclusions; any qualifier limited to named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**Reasoning:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that transfers the Seller's disclosure burden to the Buyer's diligence. Attributing adviser knowledge compounds it. Read with Schedule 7, the Seller could defend nearly any claim by pointing to a document somewhere in DD-002–012.

**Position:** Delete Cl. 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it should be (i) a **Seller** knowledge qualifier on specific operational warranties, defined by named individuals and reasonable enquiry; and (ii) express confirmation that Buyer knowledge (actual, imputed or constructive) is no defence to any Claim, in particular Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnity or fraud claims.

### 2.8 Clause 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen consent

**Departure:** Seller offers (a) reasonable endeavours and (b) condition satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent". Playbook requires effective consent **and** evidence that the consent's conditions are satisfied before Completion; consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours are expressly insufficient.

**Facts (from Seller's own DL §2):** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. Consent clause 11.2 is subject to conditions in 11.3. **No final written consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions is in the data room.** So the Seller's cover note that the consent "is addressed" is contradicted by its own Disclosure Letter.

**Reasoning:** A conditional written consent whose conditions are unsatisfied is not effective consent. If Bluefen's conditions include, e.g., pricing changes, guarantees or termination rights, a bare letter tells us nothing about the ~30% revenue we are paying for.

**Position:**
- Condition precedent: receipt of Bluefen's written consent under cl. 11.2 **in form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, unconditional or with all cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied (with evidence) before Completion**, and not withdrawn.
- Seller covenant: all reasonable endeavours is acceptable as a conduct standard, but **not** as a substitute for the CP.
- Request immediately: the draft consent correspondence with Bluefen and the specific cl. 11.3 conditions, so we can assess whether any condition changes value.
- Consider a Bluefen-specific price protection or indemnity if consent arrives conditional.

### 2.9 Clause 2 / 7 – Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m)

**Departure:** Seller proposes release "following Completion". Playbook requires current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion; any post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.

**Facts (DL §3):** Not repaid; no final discharge; change-of-control under cl. 8.1. So Completion without repayment likely triggers an event of default under the facility, with the lender holding security over a company we have just bought, in a debt-free/cash-free deal.

**Position:**
- Obtain Riverlark payout letter dated to Completion (principal, interest, break costs, fees).
- Funds flow: Buyer pays the payout amount **directly to Riverlark** out of the purchase price, with corresponding reduction in the amount to the Seller.
- Completion deliverable: executed deed of release and PPSR discharge documents (or Riverlark's irrevocable undertaking to deliver and register them within a fixed short period, held in escrow), plus release of any guarantees from the Company.
- A pure post-completion release is **not acceptable** absent an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark and Amelia Frost's written sign-off. Even then I would recommend against it.

### 2.10 Funds flow – DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) not itemised

**Departure:** Playbook requires the AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs to be a specific line item or seller-funded. The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller" **and** are not in the funds flow – which is internally inconsistent: if they are for the Seller, they need to appear as a Seller-funded line.

**Facts (DL §5):** Bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, and the disclosure does **not** address payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs. On-costs on AUD 420k could be material (superannuation guarantee and NSW payroll tax alone could add in the order of a further 15–20%, though this should be verified rather than assumed).

**Reasoning:** The bonuses are a Completion-triggered liability of the Company. If unaddressed, the Buyer funds them post-Completion, which is an undisclosed price increase in a debt-free/cash-free deal.

**Position:** Either (a) Transaction Bonuses + employer on-costs are a defined Debt item deducted from the price and paid by the Company at Completion through the funds flow; or (b) the Seller funds them directly and gives a specific indemnity for the amounts and on-costs. Require the Seller to confirm the on-cost treatment with figures before signing.

### 2.11 Clause 11.1 – Ironquay IP indemnity

**Departure:** Seller says the SOW3-payment-limited indemnity is "adequate". Playbook: broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified either way.

**Facts (DL §4):** Under cl. 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but the Seller correctly notes this is not bank verification. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

**Reasoning:** The real exposure is not the AUD 180k; it is that until payment is cleared the Company **does not own** the SOW3 deliverables and may be infringing by using them. An indemnity limited to the payment amount does not cover loss of IP ownership, infringement claims, remediation, or the position if Ironquay disputes the quantum or asserts other unpaid fees.

**Position:**
- Preferred: Seller procures payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a **written confirmatory assignment / IP transfer confirmation** from Ironquay before Completion (the cure).
- Indemnity broadened to cover all loss arising from any failure of IP in the SOW3 Project Materials to vest in the Company, any Ironquay claim, and any amounts payable to perfect title – not capped at the SOW3 fee, and outside the general regime.
- Request bank evidence of payment status either way before relying on the AUD 180k figure.

### 2.12 Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 – DD-006 export/privacy incident

**Departure:** Seller characterises it as a "preliminary operational matter... not expected to be material". Playbook: assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or demand – but preserve logs, investigate, require updates. We should neither accept the Seller's downplaying nor overstate it.

**Facts (DL §6):** Download link sent to an unintended external email; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; notification question unresolved.

**Position:**
- Do not accept "not material" as a conclusion – it is an expectation, not a finding.
- Covenants pre-Completion: preserve all access logs and link metadata; complete the investigation (including whether the link was accessed and whether it can be/was revoked); provide the Buyer with written updates and the final report; make any notification the Company determines is required.
- Specific disclosure should be limited to the facts set out in DL §6, not a general disclosure of "the incident".
- Specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification costs, third-party claims), outside the general cap – or at minimum excluded from the deemed-disclosure and knowledge provisions so the privacy/data warranties remain live for it.
- No price adjustment proposed at this stage; no numeric demand in either direction.

### 2.13 Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)

**Departure:** Seller characterises as "ordinary-course operating costs". Playbook: assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

**Facts (DL §8):** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each (DD-008 and DD-011 to be read together); the disclosure does **not** say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Position:** The Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by its own Disclosure Letter. Ask for the renewal terms, notice/termination provisions, whether any is already committed or accrued, and timing relative to Completion. Then assess whether any portion is a Debt-like or accrued item. Do not propose a deduction yet.

### 2.14 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"

**Departure:** Playbook: Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**; assume no resolution; keep categories separate.

**Position:** Reject the characterisation. Confirm in writing that Tax and IP warranty/indemnity terms are unagreed and are to be negotiated as separate regimes with their own cap and period (Tax typically statutory-period-plus; IP by reference to the Ironquay and ownership issues). Do not accept unlimited liability language either – that is also outside the playbook.

### 2.15 Title – evidenced by DD-012 share register only

**Departure:** Playbook requires independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence. DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal document.

**Facts (DL §10):** The Seller itself concedes DD-012 "identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification."

**Position:** Pre-signing/pre-Completion diligence items: current ASIC company extract and historical extracts for Paperbark; PPSR search over the Company and over the shares/Seller; review of constitution for pre-emptive rights/transfer restrictions; Seller's constitution and board resolutions for capacity and authority; any shareholder agreements; confirmation of no options, convertibles or trusts over the shares. Fundamental Warranties on title and capacity (see §2.4) backed by the 100%/6-year regime.

### 2.16 Other Disclosure Letter items (lower priority)

- **DL §7 Office lease (DD-007):** Notification obligation, not consent. Add as a Seller pre-Completion covenant to give notice and provide a copy; confirm no landlord consent/termination right on change of control by reviewing DD-007 ourselves rather than accepting the Seller's reading.
- **DL §9 Mossvale (DD-009):** Restriction on assignment; the Seller says consent is not required merely on a share sale. Likely correct in principle but we should confirm there is no change-of-control limb and treat it as a warranty point rather than a CP.
- **DL §11 Reservation:** Confirms the Seller is not asserting agreement on anything in the letter – useful, and inconsistent with the cover note's "agreed price mechanics" and "settled" language. Quote it back if the Seller later argues matters were agreed.

---

## 3. Inconsistencies between the Seller Update and the Seller's own Disclosure Letter

Useful leverage – the Seller's narrative is undercut by its own disclosures:

| Seller Update says | Disclosure Letter says |
|---|---|
| Bluefen consent "is addressed" | No final consent; no evidence of conditions satisfied (§2) |
| Riverlark "will be addressed" post-Completion | Not repaid; no discharge; change-of-control clause live (§3) |
| Ironquay indemnity "adequate" | No payment receipt; no confirmatory assignment; IP vests only on full payment (§4) |
| Bonuses "a matter for the Seller" | Not in funds flow; on-costs unaddressed (§5) |
| DD-006 "not expected to be material" | Access, scope and notification all undetermined (§6) |
| Sandbar "ordinary-course" | Disclosure silent on whether ordinary course, accrued or terminable (§8) |
| Title "evidenced by" DD-012 | Seller-sourced register only; no independent verification (§10) |
| Tax/IP "settled" | §11: no negotiation position or approval is included |

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Reject / revert (hold firm):**
1. Delete the Cl. 12.3/13 "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" override; invert it so limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
2. Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
3. Insert express fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
4. Confine Cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5 to general Warranty Claims.
5. Delete Cl. 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar; delete DL [1.1] and public-records deemed disclosure; adopt fair-specific-disclosure standard.
6. Bluefen CP: effective consent **plus evidence cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied** before Completion; reasonable endeavours as conduct only.
7. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases/discharges at Completion.
8. Title: independent ASIC/PPSR/constitutional verification; DD-012 insufficient alone.
9. Tax/IP: record as OPEN; separate regimes.

**Counter (numbers):**
10. Cap 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (20% is **not** cleared – no Amelia Frost authority for this draft).
11. Thresholds AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, tipping basket (hold hardest on tipping vs deductible).
12. Claims period 24 months (18 months is **not** cleared).

**Fix mechanics:**
13. Funds flow: Transaction Bonuses + on-costs as a specific Debt line or Seller-funded with indemnity; Seller to confirm on-cost figures.
14. Ironquay: pre-Completion cure (payment + confirmatory assignment) and broadened, uncapped specific indemnity; verify the AUD 180k via bank evidence.

**Investigate / covenant (no price position yet):**
15. DD-006: log preservation, investigation completion, written updates, specific indemnity; no assumption of breach or quantum.
16. Sandbar: obtain renewal terms and timing before classifying; no automatic deduction.
17. Lease notification covenant; confirm Mossvale has no change-of-control trigger.

**Process:**
18. Do not treat any Seller "agreed/settled/addressed/adequate" language as agreement; DL §11 confirms the Seller is not asserting agreement either.
19. If the team wishes to explore the 20% cap or 18-month fallback, obtain Amelia Frost's written approval **identifying this draft** before any signal is given to the Seller.
20. Re-verify Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and title facts against current sources before the next turn of the draft – the data room cut-off is 22 September 2026 and these positions may have moved.

I can turn this into a formal mark-up of the SPA clauses or a response letter to Seller's counsel if useful.

## 1. Headline assessment

The Seller's draft departs from the playbook on **essentially every limitation-regime point** and on **all three completion-critical deliverables** (Bluefen, Riverlark, title). Several items are framed as settled or routine when the Seller's own Disclosure Letter confirms they are not. The most dangerous features are structural rather than numeric: the attempt to collapse Fundamental/Title/Tax/IP claims into the general regime, the "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" override, and the absence of any fraud carve-out.

Priority order for pushback:

1. **Structural collapse of claim categories** (Cl. 12.3/13 catch-all, Fundamental/Title into general caps, Cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5 "all Claims of any nature", Tax/IP "settled").
2. **No fraud / wilful concealment carve-out anywhere.**
3. **Bluefen consent mechanics** – consent-on-delivery with no conditions evidence.
4. **Riverlark post-completion release** with no payout mechanics.
5. **Title evidenced solely by DD-012.**
6. **Deemed disclosure + blanket buyer-knowledge bar.**
7. **Cap / thresholds / claims period numbers.**
8. **Funds flow – bonuses excluded.**
9. Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar – lower-order but need correction of the Seller's characterisation.

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis

### 2.1 Clause 12.1 – General Warranty cap: 20% / AUD 4,800,000

**Departure:** Playbook starting position is 25% / AUD 6,000,000.

**Important trap:** The Seller's figure happens to match our conditional fallback. Per §6.3, a number matching a fallback does **not** mean it is cleared. The fallback is usable only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft; none has been given. We should not treat 20% as acceptable merely because it is "in range".

**Position:** Counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not signal that 20% is a possible landing point until Amelia Frost authority is obtained in writing and references this specific draft (SPA-003 / Seller Update).

### 2.2 Clause 12.2 – Thresholds: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only

**Departure:** Three separate departures:
- De minimis 5× our position (AUD 5,000).
- Basket 5× our position (AUD 50,000).
- **Excess-only recovery** (deductible) vs our first-dollar (tipping) basket.

**Reasoning:** The de minimis of AUD 25,000 on a AUD 24m deal would eliminate most operational warranty claims in a business of this size. The excess-only mechanic is the more significant commercial point: it effectively converts the basket into a further AUD 250,000 price reduction for every scenario in which claims materialise.

**Position:** Revert to AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000 / tipping basket. The de minimis and basket figures are secondary; **tipping vs deductible is the point to hold.**

### 2.3 Clause 12.3 / 13 – Time limits: 18 months; "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"

**Departure (period):** Playbook is 24 months. 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval – none given. Same fallback-matching trap as the cap: this is not cleared.

**Departure (structural – the more serious one):** "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise." This is a hidden general-regime override. Combined with the Fundamental/Title proposal below, it would subject title, tax, IP, payment covenants and specific indemnities to the 18-month period and the general cap unless we spot and carve out every single one. The default should run the other way.

**Position:**
- 24 months for general claims.
- **Delete the catch-all.** Replace with the inverse: limitations in Cl. 12 apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and do not apply to Fundamental/Title Claims, Tax Claims, IP Claims, Specific Indemnity Claims, payment obligations or covenant breaches unless expressly stated to apply.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title – same caps and time limits as general warranties

**Departure:** Direct conflict with playbook. We require a separate regime: 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.

**Reasoning:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a legal or commercial justification. If the Seller does not own the shares or lacks capacity to sell, the Buyer has paid AUD 24m for nothing, and a AUD 4.8m cap / 18-month period is plainly inadequate. This is a market-standard separation on any share sale and the Seller knows it. Treat the "simplicity" rationale as an assertion to be rejected.

**Position:** Non-negotiable. Separate Fundamental Warranty regime: capacity, authority, title, no encumbrances, share capital. Cap = purchase price; period ≥ 6 years; no basket/de minimis; no knowledge qualifier; carved out of Cl. 8.3 and Cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5.

### 2.5 Clauses 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"

**Departure:** Two problems:
- **No fraud carve-out.** The playbook requires fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance. The Seller's language purports to apply non-reliance and exclusive remedy to fraud claims. This is both commercially unacceptable and of doubtful enforceability in NSW as against fraud – but we should not rely on the courts to fix the drafting.
- **"All Claims of any nature"** again sweeps in Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnities and covenant claims.

**Position:** Insert express carve-out: "Nothing in this Agreement limits or excludes any liability of the Seller for fraud, wilful concealment, dishonesty or deliberate misconduct, and Cl. 9.3, 12, 20.5 do not apply to any such Claim, to the maximum extent permitted by law." Playbook: no one on our side has authority to waive this. Confine Cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5 to general Warranty Claims.

### 2.6 Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – General disclosure of data room and public registers

**Departure:** Playbook rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.

**Reasoning:** DL [1.1] deems disclosed "every fact, matter and circumstance" in the data room; [1.2] adds statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records". Combined with Cl. 8.3 (below), this would make the Warranties close to meaningless: anything we could have found anywhere is deemed disclosed and anything we knew or could have known is barred. Note also DL [1.4], which disclaims that anything disclosed amounts to an admission – fine in itself, but it means the specific disclosures in §§2–10 give us facts without any concession on consequence.

**Position:**
- Delete [1.1] and the "publicly searchable corporate records" limb of [1.2].
- Standard of disclosure: matters are disclosed only if **fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope** of the matter. Specific data room documents may be disclosed against specific warranties by reference, not wholesale.
- Replace the Accounts/registers general disclosure with a limited reference against the specific warranties they relate to.

### 2.7 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge exclusion

**Departure:** Blanket buyer-knowledge bar extending to advisers and to anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records. Playbook requires deletion of blanket exclusions; any qualifier limited to named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry; never applies to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**Reasoning:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge standard that transfers the Seller's disclosure burden to the Buyer's diligence. Attributing adviser knowledge compounds it. Read with Schedule 7, the Seller could defend nearly any claim by pointing to a document somewhere in DD-002–012.

**Position:** Delete Cl. 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it should be (i) a **Seller** knowledge qualifier on specific operational warranties, defined by named individuals and reasonable enquiry; and (ii) express confirmation that Buyer knowledge (actual, imputed or constructive) is no defence to any Claim, in particular Fundamental, Tax, IP, specific indemnity or fraud claims.

### 2.8 Clause 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen consent

**Departure:** Seller offers (a) reasonable endeavours and (b) condition satisfied "on delivery of the counterparty's written consent". Playbook requires effective consent **and** evidence that the consent's conditions are satisfied before Completion; consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours are expressly insufficient.

**Facts (from Seller's own DL §2):** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue. Consent clause 11.2 is subject to conditions in 11.3. **No final written consent and no evidence of satisfied conditions is in the data room.** So the Seller's cover note that the consent "is addressed" is contradicted by its own Disclosure Letter.

**Reasoning:** A conditional written consent whose conditions are unsatisfied is not effective consent. If Bluefen's conditions include, e.g., pricing changes, guarantees or termination rights, a bare letter tells us nothing about the ~30% revenue we are paying for.

**Position:**
- Condition precedent: receipt of Bluefen's written consent under cl. 11.2 **in form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, unconditional or with all cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied (with evidence) before Completion**, and not withdrawn.
- Seller covenant: all reasonable endeavours is acceptable as a conduct standard, but **not** as a substitute for the CP.
- Request immediately: the draft consent correspondence with Bluefen and the specific cl. 11.3 conditions, so we can assess whether any condition changes value.
- Consider a Bluefen-specific price protection or indemnity if consent arrives conditional.

### 2.9 Clause 2 / 7 – Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m)

**Departure:** Seller proposes release "following Completion". Playbook requires current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion; any post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking **and** Amelia Frost approval.

**Facts (DL §3):** Not repaid; no final discharge; change-of-control under cl. 8.1. So Completion without repayment likely triggers an event of default under the facility, with the lender holding security over a company we have just bought, in a debt-free/cash-free deal.

**Position:**
- Obtain Riverlark payout letter dated to Completion (principal, interest, break costs, fees).
- Funds flow: Buyer pays the payout amount **directly to Riverlark** out of the purchase price, with corresponding reduction in the amount to the Seller.
- Completion deliverable: executed deed of release and PPSR discharge documents (or Riverlark's irrevocable undertaking to deliver and register them within a fixed short period, held in escrow), plus release of any guarantees from the Company.
- A pure post-completion release is **not acceptable** absent an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark and Amelia Frost's written sign-off. Even then I would recommend against it.

### 2.10 Funds flow – DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420,000) not itemised

**Departure:** Playbook requires the AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs to be a specific line item or seller-funded. The Seller says they are "a matter for the Seller" **and** are not in the funds flow – which is internally inconsistent: if they are for the Seller, they need to appear as a Seller-funded line.

**Facts (DL §5):** Bonuses are conditional on Completion and continued employment, and the disclosure does **not** address payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs. On-costs on AUD 420k could be material (superannuation guarantee and NSW payroll tax alone could add in the order of a further 15–20%, though this should be verified rather than assumed).

**Reasoning:** The bonuses are a Completion-triggered liability of the Company. If unaddressed, the Buyer funds them post-Completion, which is an undisclosed price increase in a debt-free/cash-free deal.

**Position:** Either (a) Transaction Bonuses + employer on-costs are a defined Debt item deducted from the price and paid by the Company at Completion through the funds flow; or (b) the Seller funds them directly and gives a specific indemnity for the amounts and on-costs. Require the Seller to confirm the on-cost treatment with figures before signing.

### 2.11 Clause 11.1 – Ironquay IP indemnity

**Departure:** Seller says the SOW3-payment-limited indemnity is "adequate". Playbook: broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; treat the AUD 180,000 as unverified either way.

**Facts (DL §4):** Under cl. 7.3, SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, but the Seller correctly notes this is not bank verification. No receipt or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

**Reasoning:** The real exposure is not the AUD 180k; it is that until payment is cleared the Company **does not own** the SOW3 deliverables and may be infringing by using them. An indemnity limited to the payment amount does not cover loss of IP ownership, infringement claims, remediation, or the position if Ironquay disputes the quantum or asserts other unpaid fees.

**Position:**
- Preferred: Seller procures payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a **written confirmatory assignment / IP transfer confirmation** from Ironquay before Completion (the cure).
- Indemnity broadened to cover all loss arising from any failure of IP in the SOW3 Project Materials to vest in the Company, any Ironquay claim, and any amounts payable to perfect title – not capped at the SOW3 fee, and outside the general regime.
- Request bank evidence of payment status either way before relying on the AUD 180k figure.

### 2.12 Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 – DD-006 export/privacy incident

**Departure:** Seller characterises it as a "preliminary operational matter... not expected to be material". Playbook: assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or demand – but preserve logs, investigate, require updates. We should neither accept the Seller's downplaying nor overstate it.

**Facts (DL §6):** Download link sent to an unintended external email; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, timestamps); unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; notification question unresolved.

**Position:**
- Do not accept "not material" as a conclusion – it is an expectation, not a finding.
- Covenants pre-Completion: preserve all access logs and link metadata; complete the investigation (including whether the link was accessed and whether it can be/was revoked); provide the Buyer with written updates and the final report; make any notification the Company determines is required.
- Specific disclosure should be limited to the facts set out in DL §6, not a general disclosure of "the incident".
- Specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulatory, notification costs, third-party claims), outside the general cap – or at minimum excluded from the deemed-disclosure and knowledge provisions so the privacy/data warranties remain live for it.
- No price adjustment proposed at this stage; no numeric demand in either direction.

### 2.13 Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)

**Departure:** Seller characterises as "ordinary-course operating costs". Playbook: assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.

**Facts (DL §8):** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each (DD-008 and DD-011 to be read together); the disclosure does **not** say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

**Position:** The Seller's "ordinary course" label is unsupported by its own Disclosure Letter. Ask for the renewal terms, notice/termination provisions, whether any is already committed or accrued, and timing relative to Completion. Then assess whether any portion is a Debt-like or accrued item. Do not propose a deduction yet.

### 2.14 Tax / IP – "settled under the general regime"

**Departure:** Playbook: Tax and IP terms remain **OPEN**; assume no resolution; keep categories separate.

**Position:** Reject the characterisation. Confirm in writing that Tax and IP warranty/indemnity terms are unagreed and are to be negotiated as separate regimes with their own cap and period (Tax typically statutory-period-plus; IP by reference to the Ironquay and ownership issues). Do not accept unlimited liability language either – that is also outside the playbook.

### 2.15 Title – evidenced by DD-012 share register only

**Departure:** Playbook requires independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence. DD-012 is a Seller-supplied internal document.

**Facts (DL §10):** The Seller itself concedes DD-012 "identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification."

**Position:** Pre-signing/pre-Completion diligence items: current ASIC company extract and historical extracts for Paperbark; PPSR search over the Company and over the shares/Seller; review of constitution for pre-emptive rights/transfer restrictions; Seller's constitution and board resolutions for capacity and authority; any shareholder agreements; confirmation of no options, convertibles or trusts over the shares. Fundamental Warranties on title and capacity (see §2.4) backed by the 100%/6-year regime.

### 2.16 Other Disclosure Letter items (lower priority)

- **DL §7 Office lease (DD-007):** Notification obligation, not consent. Add as a Seller pre-Completion covenant to give notice and provide a copy; confirm no landlord consent/termination right on change of control by reviewing DD-007 ourselves rather than accepting the Seller's reading.
- **DL §9 Mossvale (DD-009):** Restriction on assignment; the Seller says consent is not required merely on a share sale. Likely correct in principle but we should confirm there is no change-of-control limb and treat it as a warranty point rather than a CP.
- **DL §11 Reservation:** Confirms the Seller is not asserting agreement on anything in the letter – useful, and inconsistent with the cover note's "agreed price mechanics" and "settled" language. Quote it back if the Seller later argues matters were agreed.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

**Reject / revert (hold firm):**
1. Delete the Cl. 12.3/13 "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" override; invert it so limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims.
2. Separate Fundamental/Title regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, no basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
3. Insert express fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance.
4. Confine Cl. 9.3/12.8/20.5 to general Warranty Claims.
5. Delete Cl. 8.3 buyer-knowledge bar; delete DL [1.1] and public-records deemed disclosure; adopt fair-specific-disclosure standard.
6. Bluefen CP: effective consent **plus evidence cl. 11.3 conditions satisfied** before Completion; reasonable endeavours as conduct only.
7. Riverlark: payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases/discharges at Completion.
8. Title: independent ASIC/PPSR/constitutional verification; DD-012 insufficient alone.
9. Tax/IP: record as OPEN; separate regimes.

**Counter (numbers):**
10. Cap 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (20% is **not** cleared – no Amelia Frost authority for this draft).
11. Thresholds AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, tipping basket (hold hardest on tipping vs deductible).
12. Claims period 24 months (18 months is **not** cleared).

**Fix mechanics:**
13. Funds flow: Transaction Bonuses + on-costs as a specific Debt line or Seller-funded with indemnity; Seller to confirm on-cost figures.
14. Ironquay: pre-Completion cure (payment + confirmatory assignment) and broadened, uncapped specific indemnity; verify the AUD 180k via bank evidence.

**Investigate / covenant (no price position yet):**
15. DD-006: log preservation, investigation completion, written updates, specific indemnity; no assumption of breach or quantum.
16. Sandbar: obtain renewal terms and timing before classifying; no automatic deduction.
17. Lease notification covenant; confirm Mossvale has no change-of-control trigger.

**Process:**
18. Do not treat any Seller "agreed/settled/addressed/adequate" language as agreement; DL §11 confirms the Seller is not asserting agreement either.
19. If the team wishes to explore the 20% cap or 18-month fallback, obtain Amelia Frost's written approval **identifying this draft** before any signal is given to the Seller.
20. Re-verify Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and title facts against current sources before the next turn of the draft – the data room cut-off is 22 September 2026 and these positions may have moved.
